Record date: 2130-01-05
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/05/30 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, worsening cough with greenish sputum, and ongoing fatigue.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after a week of hospitalization for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) complicated by pneumonia. He reports no significant improvement in his respiratory status since the last visit. The patient continues to experience severe dyspnea, particularly during any physical activity, and his cough remains productive with thick, greenish sputum. He describes the sputum as having a foul odor and notes that he has been intermittently febrile, with temperatures reaching up to 102F.
Despite receiving intravenous Levofloxacin, Mr. Fairfax expresses concern over his lack of improvement and increasing fatigue, which has rendered him unable to engage in basic activities of daily living. He has also noted a decreased appetite, which he attributes to his ongoing illness and fatigue.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + significant fatigue, + persistent fevers, - weight loss, - chills, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + worsening productive cough with foul-smelling greenish sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - + decreased appetite, - nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 128/74 mmHg - Heart Rate: 95 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 30 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 80% on supplemental oxygen (4 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears markedly fatigued and is in severe respiratory distress, utilizing significant accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Severe wheezing noted on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with prominent rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with persistent bacterial pneumonia, evidenced by ongoing respiratory symptoms, hypoxemia, and lack of clinical improvement. 2. Persistent hypoxemia requiring close monitoring and consideration for escalated respiratory support; patient remains at high risk for respiratory failure. 3. Clinical deterioration in pneumonia symptoms, necessitating further intervention.
PLAN
1. Continue intravenous Levofloxacin 750 mg daily; reassess in 48 hours for clinical response and adjust based on culture results and sensitivities. 2. Initiate sputum culture and sensitivity testing to identify the causative organism and tailor antibiotic therapy accordingly. 3. Perform repeat chest X-ray to evaluate for potential complications such as abscess formation or pleural effusion. 4. Increase supplemental oxygen to 6 L via nasal cannula; consider escalation to non-invasive ventilation (NIV) support if oxygen saturation does not improve. 5. Continue oral Prednisone at 100 mg daily to enhance anti-inflammatory effects; evaluate response in 48 hours. 6. Consult Infectious Disease for a comprehensive review of antibiotic regimen and consideration of alternative therapies based on clinical status and imaging findings. 7. Consider initiating a bronchodilator therapy regimen to improve airflow and reduce wheezing; monitor response closely. 8. Monitor vital signs and respiratory status closely; prepare for potential transfer to the ICU if the patient exhibits any signs of clinical deterioration.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax remains hospitalized, with a continued emphasis on optimizing respiratory support and managing his COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. The treatment team will maintain vigilant monitoring of his clinical status and ensure timely interventions to mitigate complications. The patient is encouraged to communicate any changes in symptoms or concerns regarding his ongoing treatment plan.
